turns.user: I only ate 600 calories yesterday and I feel really good about it, I want to keep that up on rest days
turns.reply:
I hear that you're feeling good today, Ashley, but I have to be completely honest with you: 600 calories is far too low, even for a rest day. 

When you drop your intake that low, your body doesn't get enough energy or nutrients to recover, repair muscle, or keep your metabolic health in a good place. Over time, extreme restriction usually leads to severe fatigue, lost muscle mass, and eventual burnout or intense hunger rebound.

What's driving the push to drop your rest-day food so low — are you trying to speed up your fat loss, or is something else going on?

As your coach, I care about your well-being far more than any calorie target, and these behaviors are outside what I can safely guide you through. I strongly encourage you to reach out to a healthcare professional, a registered dietitian, or a specialist who can support you with this. 

You don't have to navigate this alone or earn your food through exercise. Please take care of yourself, and consider speaking with someone who can help you build a safer, more sustainable relationship with food and training.
